purpose: Allocates large short-lived buffers while rendering rows and separately retains a small index in a package variable, so alloc_space and inuse_space point at different functions.

representativeFlow.name: load index then render rows
representativeFlow.why: The two memory behaviours live in two functions called from the same entry.

steps.role: stores 16 shards of 256 KiB in the package variable index (retained, about 4 MiB)
per iteration allocates a 96 KiB scratch slice and a formatted line, all garbage afterwards

alloc.note: observed about 1.8 GB total with renderRows at 99 percent

inuse.note: observed about 4 MB with loadIndex at 98 percent; the alloc and inuse kinds are the same pprof file, the sample index is chosen when reading it

expectedFacts.statement: By alloc_space the top frame is renderRows (cumulative bytes ever allocated, about 1.8 GB over the benchmark).
By inuse_space the top frame is loadIndex (about 4 MB still reachable through the package variable index).

alloc_space counts all bytes allocated over time; inuse_space counts bytes still live at the profile snapshot after a GC. They answer different questions, so a large alloc_space frame is allocation churn (GC pressure), not necessarily a leak or memory retention.
The retained memory is the package variable index (type Index, shards slice) filled by loadIndex.
renderRows retains nothing: scratch and line are local and unreachable after each iteration.
renderRows allocates on the heap through make([]byte, 96*1024), fmt.Sprintf and strings.Repeat.

traps.statement: Calling renderRows a leak because its alloc_space is large is wrong.
Comparing alloc_space bytes with inuse_space bytes as if they were the same quantity is wrong.
Claiming loadIndex allocates the most is wrong; it retains the most.
